hook: The CEO would never email you at 11pm for gift cards.
attack_scenario: CEO fraud / BEC with spoofed executive display name
defense_action: Verify payment or credential requests out-of-band using a known number

hook: 'Act in 10 minutes' is a tactic - not a deadline.
attack_scenario: Account-suspension phishing with countdown timers
defense_action: Adopt a mandatory 5-minute pause rule for urgent requests

hook: 'Everyone on your team already signed in.'
attack_scenario: Fake shared-document links and OAuth consent phishing
defense_action: Judge the sender and requested permissions - not the crowd

hook: A free favor from a stranger comes with an invoice.
attack_scenario: Vishing where the caller 'helps' first then asks for a code
defense_action: Treat unsolicited help as a flag; never read out MFA codes

hook: Say yes to something small and the big yes gets easy.
attack_scenario: Foot-in-the-door survey leading to credential request
defense_action: End the interaction when requests escalate; re-evaluate from zero

hook: Attackers study your LinkedIn so they can be your type.
attack_scenario: Spear phishing mirroring shared hobbies and alma mater
defense_action: Limit public personal detail; verify new 'friendly' contacts

hook: 'We're all in this together' is also a lure.
attack_scenario: Insider-impersonation in internal chat and helpdesk scams
defense_action: Verify identity via directory callbacks regardless of tone

hook: Click Approve 40 times and your brain stops reading.
attack_scenario: MFA push bombing (Lapsus$-style)
defense_action: Number matching and phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2)

hook: 'It won't happen to us' is the costliest sentence in security.
attack_scenario: Unpatched internet-facing devices exploited in the wild
defense_action: Patch SLAs by severity and track known-exploited CVEs

hook: Future you will fix it. Future you is busy.
attack_scenario: Reused passwords and postponed updates
defense_action: Default-on auto-update and a password manager

hook: Losses hurt about twice as much as equal gains please.
attack_scenario: Ransomware notes and 'account will be closed' lures
defense_action: Frame training around what is protected - not only punished

hook: Analysts find what they expect to find.
attack_scenario: SOC anchoring on first hypothesis; missed lateral movement
defense_action: Assign a devil's advocate and log disconfirming evidence

hook: The first number you see quietly sets the price of risk.
attack_scenario: Risk scoring inflated or deflated by the first estimate
defense_action: Collect estimates independently before sharing

hook: 'You won't believe who viewed your profile.'
attack_scenario: USB drops and QR-code phishing (quishing)
defense_action: Never plug in or scan unknown media; use sandboxed analysis

hook: A logo and a polished page borrow trust they have not earned.
attack_scenario: Cloned brand portals and fake vendor sites
defense_action: Check domain and certificate context; bookmark real portals

hook: We trust what we have seen before - even in a scam.
attack_scenario: Typosquatted domains and lookalike senders
defense_action: Hover to inspect; use allow-listed domains and DMARC

hook: Last week's training fades by Friday.
attack_scenario: Phishing success after a long gap since training
defense_action: Run short just-in-time refreshers after real incidents

hook: Everything has been fine so far - until it isn't.
attack_scenario: No tested backups or IR plan until breach day
defense_action: Run tabletop exercises and restore drills quarterly

hook: 'I'd never fall for that' is what victims said first.
attack_scenario: Senior staff clicking sophisticated lures
defense_action: Normalize reporting; measure report rate not click shame

hook: Choosing your own password feels safer than a random one.
attack_scenario: Predictable human-chosen passwords
defense_action: Use generated passphrases and passkeys

hook: Forty people saw the odd email. Zero reported it.
attack_scenario: Unreported phishing campaigns inside an org
defense_action: One-click report button with fast feedback

hook: Shared ownership of security equals owned by nobody.
attack_scenario: Orphaned cloud assets and unmanaged shadow IT
defense_action: Assign named owners to every asset and control

hook: After a breach everything looks obvious.
attack_scenario: Blame-heavy postmortems hiding systemic causes
defense_action: Use blameless postmortems and decision logs

hook: We fear the breach we read about - not the one we are exposed to.
attack_scenario: Over-investing in headline threats while ignoring misconfigurations
defense_action: Prioritise by exposure and likelihood data

hook: One scary alert hides ten thousand harmless ones.
attack_scenario: Misjudged detection precision and false-positive load
defense_action: Calculate precision with base rates before tuning alerts

hook: We study the breaches that got reported.
attack_scenario: Security metrics built only from detected incidents
defense_action: Include near-misses and undetected risk estimates

hook: We keep the failing tool because we paid for it.
attack_scenario: Legacy security product retained despite coverage gaps
defense_action: Evaluate controls on forward value only

hook: Default settings win by doing nothing.
attack_scenario: Default credentials and open storage buckets
defense_action: Ship secure-by-default and audit drift

hook: Opt-out beats opt-in by a landslide.
attack_scenario: MFA adoption lagging when optional
defense_action: Enforce MFA by default for new accounts

hook: Security projects take twice as long as planned.
attack_scenario: Patch or migration deadlines repeatedly missed
defense_action: Use reference-class forecasting and add buffer

hook: Feeling safer makes us act riskier.
attack_scenario: Staff relaxing behavior after EDR or MFA rollout
defense_action: Communicate that tools reduce - not remove - risk

hook: Repeat a lie often enough and it feels familiar.
attack_scenario: Disinformation and fake breach rumours
defense_action: Pause and verify with primary sources

hook: We blame the person - not the broken process.
attack_scenario: Blaming users who click instead of fixing mail filtering
defense_action: Fix the system first then train

hook: Confidence peaks right before the learning curve bites.
attack_scenario: Over-trusting self-taught security fixes in production
defense_action: Peer review and staged rollout for security changes

hook: The tool said it was fine so we stopped thinking.
attack_scenario: Blind trust in scanner or AI output
defense_action: Verify high-impact findings manually

hook: Overloaded people choose the fastest option - not the safest.
attack_scenario: Phishing during peak workloads or end of month
defense_action: Reduce friction on the secure path and avoid peak-time pressure

hook: Twenty-five security options and everyone picks none.
attack_scenario: Misconfigured settings from too many toggles
defense_action: Offer two clear recommended presets

hook: Tell people not to - and they will.
attack_scenario: Shadow IT after blanket blocking
defense_action: Explain the why and offer a sanctioned alternative

hook: A harmless question today. A password tomorrow.
attack_scenario: Multi-stage pretexting calls
defense_action: Treat small info requests as reconnaissance

hook: The outrageous ask makes the real ask feel fair.
attack_scenario: Escalating wire request then a 'smaller' fraud
defense_action: Evaluate each request on its own merits

hook: Holding the door is kindness - and an attack path.
attack_scenario: Physical tailgating into offices
defense_action: Badge-in policy and a polite way to say no

hook: People want to help. Attackers know it.
attack_scenario: Helpdesk password-reset social engineering
defense_action: Scripted verification that does not depend on mood

hook: Free money and free movies are never free.
attack_scenario: Advance-fee and fake-prize scams
defense_action: Ask what the sender gains - then verify independently

hook: Victims who bend rules are easier to blackmail.
attack_scenario: Sextortion and illicit-offer baits
defense_action: Report early - the shame is the attacker's leverage

hook: While you watch the fire alarm they take the badge.
attack_scenario: Distraction-based vishing and pickpocket-style social attacks
defense_action: Slow down when something sudden demands attention

hook: If everyone else is doing it the risk feels outsourced.
attack_scenario: Mass-shared malicious browser extensions
defense_action: Check permissions and publisher history

hook: A ticking clock shuts down careful thinking.
attack_scenario: Fake deadline invoices and gift-card scams
defense_action: Write down the real deadline and who set it

hook: One changed bank detail cost a company six figures.
attack_scenario: Vendor email compromise and altered remittance details
defense_action: Call-back verification and dual approval over a threshold

hook: The attacker only needed one tired 'Approve'.
attack_scenario: Push bombing combined with a helpdesk call
defense_action: Number matching and rate limits on pushes

hook: Support staff are the new perimeter.
attack_scenario: Attacker calls IT to reset MFA for a stolen account
defense_action: Strong identity proofing before any reset

hook: A QR code hides the URL from your filters and your eyes.
attack_scenario: QR in email or on parking meters leading to credential pages
defense_action: Preview the URL; avoid scanning codes from unsolicited sources

hook: The voice sounded exactly right.
attack_scenario: AI-cloned voice authorising a transfer
defense_action: Use code words and call-back on a known number

hook: No password was stolen - you just granted access.
attack_scenario: Malicious OAuth app requesting mail and file scope
defense_action: Admin consent controls and app review

hook: Your phone number is the weakest key you own.
attack_scenario: Carrier social engineering to hijack SMS codes
defense_action: Move off SMS MFA; set carrier PIN lock

hook: The popup is a picture of a popup.
attack_scenario: Fake login window drawn inside a page
defense_action: Drag the window - if it will not leave the page it is fake

hook: 'Verify you are human' by pasting a command? Run.
attack_scenario: Fake CAPTCHA tricking users into running PowerShell
defense_action: Never paste commands from a webpage; restrict Run dialog

hook: The recruiter's coding test is the malware.
attack_scenario: Trojanised take-home assignments targeting developers
defense_action: Open tests only in a throwaway VM

hook: Maintainers are people with limited time.
attack_scenario: Social engineering of open-source maintainers for access
defense_action: Two-person review and signed releases

hook: The romance lasted weeks. The loss lasted years.
attack_scenario: Long-con crypto investment fraud via messaging apps
defense_action: Never invest on advice from a chat-only relationship

hook: A missed parcel text is a pre-approved pretext.
attack_scenario: SMS with a delivery fee link
defense_action: Go to the carrier's app directly - never the text link

hook: Make the safe thing easy and the unsafe thing slightly annoying.
attack_scenario: Download warnings that users skip
defense_action: Use contextual warnings with clear action labels

hook: Pre-commit your future self.
attack_scenario: Planned patch windows with leadership sign-off
defense_action: Automated enforcement of agreed maintenance windows

hook: '9 in 10 of your peers reported this email' works better than a threat.
attack_scenario: Low phishing report rates
defense_action: Show peer reporting stats in awareness messages

hook: If-then plans beat good intentions.
attack_scenario: Staff who know but do not act
defense_action: Teach 'If I get an urgent request then I call to verify'

hook: Teach at the moment of the mistake.
attack_scenario: Clicking a simulated phish then waiting a month for feedback
defense_action: Instant micro-lesson after a click

hook: Thank the person who reported - publicly.
attack_scenario: Silence after reports reduces future reporting
defense_action: Fast acknowledgment and a visible leaderboard of helpers

hook: Imagine it already failed - now say why.
attack_scenario: Launching controls without failure analysis
defense_action: Run a 30-minute pre-mortem before big rollouts

hook: A strength meter is a nudge. A banned-password list is a wall.
attack_scenario: Weak passwords accepted by policy
defense_action: Block breached passwords and allow long passphrases

hook: Users are not the weakest link - bad design is.
attack_scenario: Blaming individuals for system failures
defense_action: Design for human behavior and treat users as sensors

hook: Click rate alone is a vanity metric.
attack_scenario: Gamed phishing simulations
defense_action: Track report rate and time-to-report instead

hook: Length beats symbols - and forced rotation backfires.
attack_scenario: Policy forcing frequent resets
defense_action: Adopt long passphrases and breach checks

hook: Your identity is the product.
attack_scenario: Credential stuffing and account resale
defense_action: Unique passwords and MFA everywhere

topic: Only gullible people fall for scams
hook: Scam success tracks timing and stress - not intelligence.
attack_scenario: Victim blaming that suppresses reporting
defense_action: Promote a no-shame reporting culture

topic: Voice cloning and the verification gap
hook: Hearing is no longer believing.
attack_scenario: Cloned voice of a relative or executive
defense_action: Family or team safe words and call-back

hook: Your AI assistant can be socially engineered too.
attack_scenario: Hidden instructions in web pages or emails read by agents
defense_action: Constrain agent permissions and require human approval

hook: Bad grammar is no longer the red flag.
attack_scenario: LLM-written fluent spearphish
defense_action: Verify intent and channel instead of spotting typos

hook: Fluent does not mean correct.
attack_scenario: Pasting AI-suggested commands or code blindly
defense_action: Review and test before running

hook: The candidate on camera may not be the candidate.
attack_scenario: Fake remote workers with stolen or synthetic identities
defense_action: Live ID checks and structured identity verification

hook: Not everyone online is who they say they are.
attack_scenario: Grooming and fake friend profiles in games
defense_action: Teach: never share location; tell a trusted adult

hook: Free robux is never free.
attack_scenario: Fake in-game currency generators
defense_action: Ask a parent before clicking or entering any account details

hook: Being kind does not mean saying yes to everything.
attack_scenario: Asking kids to keep a secret or share a code
defense_action: Teach a 'secrets that make you uneasy get shared' rule

hook: Stop. Think. Ask.
attack_scenario: Pop-up prizes and fake virus warnings
defense_action: Teach a three-step pause habit

hook: A password is a toothbrush: do not share it and change it when needed.
attack_scenario: Friends sharing passwords at school
defense_action: Use a password manager with parents

hook: A family safe word beats a perfect deepfake.
attack_scenario: Voice-cloned 'emergency' calls
defense_action: Agree on a family code word and never post it

hook: People report mistakes only if it is safe to.
attack_scenario: Employees hiding clicks until damage spreads
defense_action: Leaders model fast disclosure and no punishment for reporting

hook: Peer influence beats policy memos.
attack_scenario: Awareness programs with no local advocates
defense_action: Recruit champions in each team

hook: Measure what people do - not what they remember.
attack_scenario: Training completion used as the KPI
defense_action: Track report rate and repeat-risk behaviors

hook: Scare without a solution produces denial.
attack_scenario: Fear-heavy campaigns with no clear action
defense_action: Pair threat with an efficacy-building action

hook: Too many demands and people stop complying.
attack_scenario: Policy overload leading to workarounds
defense_action: Reduce required decisions and automate secure defaults

hook: Users protect what they imagine is at risk.
attack_scenario: Staff think only large firms are targeted
defense_action: Use concrete stories relevant to their role
